wallet.name: Wallets & signatures
wallet.short: A wallet holds a key pair: a public *address* that anyone can pay, and a private key that *signs* approvals and never leaves the device.

signature.name: Signatures
signature.short: Every transaction is signed by the wallets it spends from. The first signature doubles as the transaction's ID, which is what your code gets back and looks up later.

transaction.name: Transactions
transaction.short: A transaction is a signed request to change the shared ledger. It either fully happens or doesn't happen at all, and once confirmed anyone can look it up.

account.name: Accounts
account.short: Everything on Solana (balances, tokens, programs, app data) lives in accounts: records at an address, each with an owner that is allowed to change it.

clusters.name: Devnet & mainnet
clusters.short: Devnet is a free public test network that behaves like the real one (mainnet), with play money. Same code, different URL.

token-account.name: Token accounts
token-account.short: Wallets don't hold tokens directly. Each token (USDC, or your own asset) gets a small account owned by the wallet, and transfers move between these accounts.

mint.name: Mints & authorities
mint.short: A mint account defines a token: its supply, its decimals, who may create more (*mint authority*), and who may freeze holders (*freeze authority*).

extensions.name: Token extensions
extensions.short: Optional features of the Token-2022 program, such as metadata, pausing, default-frozen accounts, and transfer hooks, switched on per mint. Most must be chosen **when the mint is created**.

fees.name: Fees
fees.short: Every transaction pays a small flat network fee, currently a fraction of a cent, whatever the amount. The transaction's fee payer pays, and that can be your app rather than your customer.

sponsorship.name: Fee sponsorship
sponsorship.short: By default, the transaction's fee payer needs a little SOL to pay its fee. A fee-payer service such as Kora lets your app pay instead, so customers only ever hold dollars.

rent.name: Rent (storage deposit)
rent.short: Every account holds a small refundable deposit for the space it takes up. Opening a USDC account for a new customer costs about 0.0015 SOL, which comes back if the account is closed.

commitment.name: Confirmation & finality
commitment.short: A transaction goes from *processed* to *finalized* in well under a second, and once finalized it can't be reversed. *Confirmed* reports the same block as finalized.

rpc.name: RPC
rpc.short: RPC is the HTTP/JSON API your code uses to read from and send to the network. Use public endpoints for testing and a provider in production.

program.name: Programs
program.short: Programs are code deployed to the network that owns and updates accounts. Most apps call existing programs, such as the Token program, rather than writing their own.

pda.name: Program-derived addresses
pda.short: A PDA is an address derived from a program plus some seeds. It has no private key, so only that program can sign for it, which makes it handy for storing app state at predictable addresses.

cpi.name: Cross-program calls
cpi.short: A cross-program call (CPI) is one program calling another inside the same transaction, the way your program would call the Token program to move tokens.
